bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Weather volatility impacting domestic demand; prolonged regulatory delays in biologicals outside India; biotech funding slowdown affecting pharma CDMO conversions; Chinese overcapacity depressing global agchem prices; geopolitical uncertainty around U.S. tariffs

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes strategic momentum in new products, pharma pipeline, and biologicals; confident in FY26 recovery from Q4 and long-term transformation into diversified life sciences player
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Contract assets of Rs. 450 Cr represent revenue already recognized but deferred delivery — not inventory, signaling strong customer commitment despite market softness; biologicals revenue is small ($12M) but has 25%+ CAGR potential and unique peptide platform
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt-free balance sheet described as positioning the company to navigate volatility and invest in future growth businesses; debt/equity ratio of 0.02 as at Jun-26 (0.01 at Jun-25).
- Surplus cash net of debt of INR 37,939 Mn, described as a 'war chest of growth capital' enabling pursuit of future strategic investments for long-term sustainable growth.
- Trade working capital reduced by 19 days to 120 days in Jun-26; NWC days moved from 139 (Q4FY26) to 120 (Q1FY27), with inventory DIO 66 to 71, receivables DSO 126 to 112 and payables DPO 53 to 63.
- Strategy is explicitly 'prudent capital allocation to ensure long-term shareholder value creation', combining organic growth with inorganic value creation - continuing evaluation of inorganic opportunities in the long term, targeting niche verticals within pharma/specialty chemicals and high-growth application areas having synergy.
- Shareholders' fund of INR 1,14,683 Mn at Jun-26 versus INR 1,06,003 Mn at Jun-25; net sales to net fixed assets ratio has fallen to 1.30 (Jun-26) from 1.75 (Jun-25) as the asset base builds ahead of revenue.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated in-house R&D platform: 700+ scientists, 200+ PhDs and a proprietary library of 80,000+ compounds, with end-to-end capabilities across discovery, process development, formulation and manufacturing
- Active pipeline of over 90 molecules, described as among the strongest in the Company's history, with more than 60% in advanced stages of development
- Ranked among the top five globally in Custom Synthesis and Manufacturing, built on three decades of trust, technical depth and complex chemistry
- Proprietary IP origination: Pioxaniliprole is the first insecticide molecule developed by an Indian company to receive ISO approval, and the first time an Indian company plans to take a novel active ingredient from original discovery through to global commercialisation
- Long-term partnerships with global innovators for complex, early-stage and patented molecules rather than transactional engagements, supporting margin resilience
- Proprietary biological IP through the Plant Health Care (now PI AgSciences) acquisition, including PREtec peptide technology and regulatory credentials in the US, Brazil, Mexico, Spain and the UK
- Advanced manufacturing capability - continuous flow, safer phosgenation, green catalyst and biotechnology platforms; proof-of-concepts for advanced drying (RDDC) and liquid-liquid extraction demonstrated up to 40% energy savings and a 15% reduction in batch cycle times
- Enterprise-wide digital backbone: went live on SAP S/4HANA across a multi-business, multi-geography footprint
- ESG standing: featured for the third consecutive year in the S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook, ranking among the top 2 percentile of ESG-rated companies worldwide, with CSA score rising from 68 to 77, and inclusion in the Dow Jones Best in Class Indices for Emerging Markets
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Prolonged cyclical downturn and inventory correction in the global crop protection market — The global crop protection market has witnessed a prolonged cyclical downturn shaped by industry-wide inventory corrections; consolidated AgChem exports declined 19% in FY2026 and consolidated revenue fell 16% YoY, showing how directly the cycle transmits to the top line.
- Dependence on global innovator partners' offtake schedules — Revenue moderation was attributed primarily to deferred offtake schedules by global innovator partners and inventory rationalisation across key markets - delivery phasing sits with the customer, not the Company, so revenue timing is only partly controllable.
- Weather and monsoon dependence in the domestic business — The monsoon season, influenced by La Nina conditions, produced unseasonal and erratic rainfall that adversely impacted crop cycles and farm productivity; abiotic stress (weather) acted as a major headwind that lowered sales volume in the Domestic segment.
- Regulatory action on the product portfolio, particularly biologicals — The business environment was challenged by a regulatory ban on biologicals and by regulatory transitions in biologicals, which disrupted domestic demand during the year.
- Raw-material price volatility — Continued volatility in input costs and volatile raw-material prices are cited as ongoing pressures on the cost base alongside the demand downturn.
- Pricing pressure in generic agrochemicals — Pricing pressures in the generic agrochemicals segment were named as a driver of revenue moderation, indicating limited pricing power outside differentiated and patented molecules.
- Farmer economic stress and working-capital constraints in the trade channel — Economic stress on farmers led to demand disruption and significant value erosion across the crop protection industry, with working-capital constraints in trade further challenging the domestic environment.
- Process safety and occupational health hazards in chemical manufacturing — The BRSR discloses an employee LTIFR of 0.29 per million person-hours and one high-consequence work-related injury in FY 2025-26 (nil in FY 2025), with the risk managed through HAZOP/What-If studies, HIRA/JSA, Pre-Startup Safety Reviews, LOTO, permit-to-work, third-party Quantitative Risk Assessments and Critical Risk Identification exercises.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Top 5 worldwide in AgChem CSM with 70%+ of revenue from proprietary products; 6+ decades of work with global innovators and 'zero conflicts till date' under a non-conflicting business model.
- Deck frames a staged transformation - 1961 leading agri distribution player, 1995 top 5 global CSM player, 2020 innovation-led Agsciences, 2025 onward Agsciences to Lifesciences (through 2030) - labelling ~20% reported revenue CAGR at each stage.
- 'Right to win' rests on innovation mindset, global partnership, strong balance sheet and execution excellence; the company describes itself as never a 'me-too' player with new frontiers in Agri, Horticulture, Biologicals and Health Sciences.
- Differentiated domestic distribution model built on 25+ global innovators, more than 6 decades of market-leading brand creation (some brands more than a decade old) and experience managing the transition of products from patented to generic.
- Featured in the S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook for the 3rd consecutive year and included in the Dow Jones Best in Class (DJ BIC) Indices for Emerging Markets.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demand cycle] Deck acknowledges cyclical headwinds: soft demand in the global agrochemical industry, generics pressure continuing with global agrochemical companies, pricing under pressure, and delayed and uneven monsoon impacting Kharif sowing and partially postponing domestic sales.
- [Input costs] Increase in input material prices due to ongoing geopolitical tensions impacted gross margin, though the deck also states commodity prices are showing a positive trend.
- [CRDMO headwinds] PI Health Sciences faces a slowdown in biotech funding and geopolitical challenges, with the Q1FY27 revenue decline attributed mainly to customer order phasing; the deck reports PIHS revenue contracted 25% YoY and PIHS remains loss-making at the PBT level post intercompany eliminations.
- [Order book] Order book is said to continue supporting the growth outlook for new products in FY27, with build-up of pipeline projects through new strategic partnerships entered in the last 12 months and improved business development and R&D pipeline visibility over the next 1-2 years.
- [Awards] India's Top Value Creator 2025 - Agro Chemicals by Dun & Bradstreet; Most Preferred Workplace 2025-26 by Marksmen Daily; British Safety Council Sword of Honour for the Udaipur site (October 2025); Business Leader of the Year - ESG at Chemtech Leadership & Excellence Awards 2026.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: PI Industries manufactures and distributes agro chemicals and operates through a single reportable business segment, 'Agro Chemicals', serving both domestic and international markets with customers ranging from institutional buyers to end consumers. Its core model is custom synthesis and manufacturing for global agrochemical innovators built on complex process chemistry, alongside a domestic branded crop-protection business. During the year the Company continued its transition from a pure agri-chemical company to a diversified life sciences enterprise, extending into pharmaceutical, global biologicals and specialty / electronic chemicals.

outlook.body:
- Capital allocation on a balanced, multi-track approach: R&D and strategic capex for manufacturing expansion and new-business scale-up, selective acquisitions to strengthen capabilities and technology, and sustained returns to shareholders
- Continue the transition from a pure agri-chemical company to a diversified life sciences enterprise extending into pharmaceutical, global biologicals and specialty / electronic chemicals
- Deepen the CSM model of long-term, IP-driven partnerships with global AgChem innovators on complex process chemistry, and commercialise new molecules to support gross-margin expansion
- Build PI Health Sciences as a CRDMO partner for global pharma and biotech innovators, anchored on the Hyderabad CRO facility and the Lodi (Italy) kilo-lab
- Scale the Biologicals platform globally through PI AgSciences (formerly Plant Health Care) across the USA, Brazil, Mexico, Spain and the UK using its proprietary technology
- Reposition the domestic Agri Brands portfolio through new product launches and a 20+ product development pipeline
- Digitalise the operating backbone - live on SAP S/4HANA under Project INDRA as a single system of record for procurement, planning, inventory and financial reporting
- Talent strategy built on three pillars: attracting scientific and commercial talent across geographies, capability development through training, rotational programmes and laboratory access, and fostering a culture of innovation and ownership
- Operate an integrated Enterprise Risk Management framework built on leading global frameworks and tailored to the Company's business model and geographic footprint
- Occupational Health and Safety Management System aligned with ISO 45001 implemented across all five manufacturing sites and the R&D facility, covering employees, contract workers, visitors and other relevant stakeholders
- 100% of plants and offices assessed during FY 2025-26 for Health & Safety and for Working Conditions
- Zero fatalities among employees and workers in FY 2025-26 and FY 2025; LTIFR for all employees and workers including contractual reported at 0.10, with no reportable safety incidents recorded during FY 2025-26 per the HSEMS disclosure
- Reasonable Assurance obtained from Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP, an external agency, on the disclosed safety indicators
- Structured grievance redressal mechanism with a Grievance Redressal Committee comprising management and worker representatives, covering permanent, contractual and third-party personnel, and extended to value-chain partners through audits and annual supplier meets
- Equal Opportunity Policy in accordance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, applied across recruitment, role assignment, compensation, promotions, transfers and professional development
- Health & safety and skill-upgradation training coverage of 99.51% and 99.40% of employees and 100% of workers in FY 2025-26
- 100% return-to-work rate for permanent employees taking parental leave (77% total retention rate)
- Integrated Health, Safety and Environment Management System supported by an independent OHS function, inter-site safety audits, Safety Circle cross-functional reviews and third-party Quantitative Risk Assessments feeding on-site emergency response plans
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Capital deployment in FY 2025-26 was directed towards manufacturing expansion, R&D infrastructure and Pharma CRDMO facilities, with the Company stating that '₹11,508 million of capex deployed towards manufacturing expansion, R&D infrastructure and Pharma CRDMO facilities, including capacity additions at Jambusar, Panoli, Jaipur and Lodi (Italy)'. In pharma, the CRO facility in Hyderabad strengthens discovery and development capability while the commissioning of the kilo-lab facility in Lodi, Italy is expected to enhance the ability to serve global pharmaceutical customers; the pharma vertical is described as progressively transitioning from a development-stage CRDMO to a commercial-stage, revenue-generating business, with capabilities extending to ADCs and large molecules under evaluation. The Biologicals platform expanded its global presence across the US, Brazil, Mexico, UK and Europe on the peptide technology platform, with a bio-nematicide registration approved in the U.S. and a differentiated biological nematode solution commercially launched in Mexico; the Seattle R&D Centre serves as the global hub for innovation, field validation, product development and commercial support. On the manufacturing footprint the Company is advancing towards a smart-factory model and digital lighthouse designation aligned with Industry 4.0, executing no/low-touch manufacturing, digitalisation and automation initiatives, smart steam-trap retrofits and a smart fuel monitoring system, alongside heat pumps, energy-efficient screw chillers and automated flow controllers; waste-stream recycling scale-up eliminated downstream utility loads for distillation and Multi-Effect Evaporator operations while capturing 10-30% specific energy savings. Renewable energy rose to over 10.0% of total electricity consumption, water interventions (dry vacuum pumps replacing steam jet ejectors, RO efficiency, Sewage Treatment Plants) delivered a 68% increase in water recycling and recovery volume and lowered total wastewater generation by 16% towards zero-liquid-discharge objectives, and following biodiversity risk assessments across all operational sites and R&D centres, plans are finalised to develop a dedicated biodiversity park featuring over 100,000 native saplings in FY27.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management remains optimistic about the medium- to long-term outlook; early signals from global innovator partners - indicative offtake plans and a stabilised order book - suggest industry inventory normalisation is underway
- Healthy reservoir levels entering Kharif FY2026-27 and a stabilised domestic biologicals portfolio following regulatory disruptions position the Company to benefit from improving market conditions
- The AgChem business is expected to maintain strong momentum, driven by a healthy order book, a robust pipeline of commercialised and late-stage molecules and deepening partnerships with global innovators
- FY 2025-26 was marked by cyclical revenue headwinds across the global AgChem sector, with revenue trajectory hit by moderated AgChem exports amid customer scheduling, plus erratic weather and regulatory transitions in biologicals domestically
- Gross-margin support from mix: new products contributed 18% of AgChem Exports revenue and five new molecules were commercialised during the year (15+ over three years)
- Global CRDMO market was valued at approximately USD 196 billion in 2023 and is projected to reach approximately USD 329 billion by 2029, growing at a CAGR of about 9.0%, as global biotech and pharma increase outsourcing driven by pipeline complexity, capital-efficiency requirements and the need for specialised capabilities
- PI Health Sciences revenue grew 40% YoY with positive momentum through new partnerships and an expanded active customer base
- Biologicals demand opening: US EPA registration and commercial launch of PI's foliar bionematicide, the world's first foliar-application nematode product, creates a new use-case model for nematode management in standing crops
- Domestic Agri Brands performance was mixed, impacted by adverse weather, lower crop prices, regulatory disruptions in biologicals and elevated channel inventory
- Government schemes extending affordable institutional credit to smallholder farmers can support a gradual improvement in effective demand for quality agrochemical products, including branded, differentiated and biological crop-protection solutions
- In FY 2025-26 the CSM order book held steady, indicating an intact pipeline
- A stabilised order book and indicative offtake plans from global innovator partners are cited as early signals of inventory normalisation
- R&D pipeline of 90+ molecules supported by 700+ scientists across 4 R&D centres
- Agri Brands: four new products launched with a strong pipeline of 20+ products at different stages of development
- PI Health Sciences conversion of development-stage engagements is anchored on a growing late-stage clinical pipeline

deepdive.thesis: Despite H1 revenue decline due to weather and regulatory headwinds, PI is on track with 8-10 new product launches, strong pharma CDMO pipeline, and biologicals recovery in Q4; the shift from AgChem-only to diversified life sciences is accelerating, with non-AgChem segments now contributing meaningfully.

open.item: Following biodiversity risk assessments across all operational sites and R&D centres, plans are finalised to develop a dedicated biodiversity park featuring over 100,000 native saplings in FY27 (a trackable dated environmental project rather than a financial or capacity commitment).
Aspires to significantly scale the global Biologicals business over the next five years, supported by two newly commissioned R&D centres in India and the US.
Ambition to build a leading global CRDMO through PI Health Sciences over the medium term, spanning discovery to commercialisation with an R&D centre in Hyderabad and manufacturing in India and Italy.
Plans to take Pioxaniliprole, its proprietary novel active ingredient, from original discovery through to global commercialisation - stated as a first for an Indian company.

PI NEXT is the stated strategic frame for the next phase: from selling products to owning outcomes, from individual leadership to institutional capability and from operational excellence to business excellence powered by science, IP, platforms and digital infrastructure.
Strengthen the AgChem Exports order book and innovator relationships to support export volume recovery as inventory normalisation progresses, subject to customer delivery schedules.
Commercialise Pioxaniliprole - domestic commercial launch of India's first new chemical entity, subject to regulatory approval, and initiate global regulatory filings in select geographies.
Achieve PI Health Sciences revenue scale by converting development-stage engagements into long-term commercial supply agreements, anchored on the growing late-stage clinical pipeline.
Scale up Global Biologicals by strengthening the go-to-market approach anchored on geography-specific distribution, farmer outreach and field-level efficacy demonstrations to accelerate adoption.
Expand non-AgChem by continuing to build specialty chemicals and electronic chemicals enquiries in the new-business pipeline.
Improve asset utilisation by driving higher throughput across existing manufacturing facilities through product-mix optimisation and operational-efficiency programmes.
Optimise working capital through disciplined receivables and inventory management to strengthen cash flow and balance sheet resilience.

Direct capital on a multi-track basis towards R&D and strategic capex for manufacturing expansion and new-business scale-up, selective acquisitions to strengthen capabilities and technology, and sustained shareholder returns, while retaining flexibility for selective strategic acquisitions across AgChem, Biologicals, Pharma CRDMO and Specialty & Electronic Chemicals.
Commissioning of the kilo-lab facility at Lodi, Italy is expected to enhance PI Health Sciences' ability to serve global pharmaceutical customers.

Firm commitment to ensuring 100% procurement from sources free from Child Labour and Forced Labour, in alignment with national regulations and international labour standards, while maintaining 99% key supplier declaration coverage.

The pharma vertical is being transitioned from a development-stage CRDMO to a commercial-stage, revenue-generating business as a key strategic growth platform over the medium term, with capabilities in ADCs and large molecules under evaluation.

risks.note: The global crop protection market has witnessed a prolonged cyclical downturn shaped by industry-wide inventory corrections; consolidated AgChem exports declined 19% in FY2026 and consolidated revenue fell 16% YoY, showing how directly the cycle transmits to the top line.
risks.risk: Prolonged cyclical downturn and inventory correction in the global crop protection market

risks.note: Revenue moderation was attributed primarily to deferred offtake schedules by global innovator partners and inventory rationalisation across key markets - delivery phasing sits with the customer, not the Company, so revenue timing is only partly controllable.
risks.risk: Dependence on global innovator partners' offtake schedules

risks.note: The monsoon season, influenced by La Nina conditions, produced unseasonal and erratic rainfall that adversely impacted crop cycles and farm productivity; abiotic stress (weather) acted as a major headwind that lowered sales volume in the Domestic segment.
risks.risk: Weather and monsoon dependence in the domestic business

risks.note: The business environment was challenged by a regulatory ban on biologicals and by regulatory transitions in biologicals, which disrupted domestic demand during the year.
risks.risk: Regulatory action on the product portfolio, particularly biologicals

risks.note: Continued volatility in input costs and volatile raw-material prices are cited as ongoing pressures on the cost base alongside the demand downturn.
Pricing pressures in the generic agrochemicals segment were named as a driver of revenue moderation, indicating limited pricing power outside differentiated and patented molecules.

Economic stress on farmers led to demand disruption and significant value erosion across the crop protection industry, with working-capital constraints in trade further challenging the domestic environment.
risks.risk: Farmer economic stress and working-capital constraints in the trade channel
